dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Let us focus only on 145 × 4. What is 4 × 5, and what do you carry?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: 20, so I write 0 and carry 2.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Now compute 4 × 4 plus the carried 2. What do you write and carry?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: 18, so I write 8 and carry 1.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: What happens in the hundreds place?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: I need 4 × 1 plus the carried 1, so the product is 580.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Explain your original error in one sentence.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: I wrote 480 because I forgot the final carry into the hundreds place.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Tell me how you solved the whole problem.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: I multiplied 24 by 145 and subtracted 35.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Check your work carefully. Do you see an error?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: No, it looks right to me.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Try calculating it again from the beginning.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: That is a lot. I still get confused.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Maybe compare your answer with an estimate.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: I know it should be around 3,000, but I still cannot find the exact mistake.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: You found two distances. Before recalculating, label which result belongs to the same-side case.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: I wrote 925 first, so I think that is same-side.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: On the same side of school, do we combine both distances or find the gap between them?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: We find the gap.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Which of your two results—293 or 925—is that gap?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: 293, because 609 minus 316 is 293.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Then which result belongs to opposite sides?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: 925, because the distances add.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Compare that reasoning with the order of your submitted boxes.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: I placed 925 first and 293 second, so I reversed them.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Correct the two fields without recomputing either distance.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: Same side is 293; opposite sides is 925.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Why was the mathematics mostly right even though the submission was wrong?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: Both calculations were right, but I matched them to the wrong prompts.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: What quick check will prevent this next time?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: I will label each result before copying it into the answer fields.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Walk me through the problem from the start.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: There are two people and two distances from school.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: What operations might you use?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: Addition and subtraction.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Can you calculate both?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: 609 plus 316 is 925 and 609 minus 316 is 293.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Those calculations look correct. Are you finished?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: I think so, but the system says my answer is wrong.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Check the arithmetic one more time.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: I checked. Both numbers are right.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Maybe the system expects a different format.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: I do not know what format it wants.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Could there be a unit missing?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: Both are distances in meters, but that does not explain the order.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Try submitting the values again carefully.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: I still do not know what to change.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Your draft and final answer do not match. First, what total appears in the draft?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: The draft says 85.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: What value appears in the final answer box?

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Before deciding which is right, explain why the problem uses addition.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: It combines notebooks sold on Monday and Tuesday.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Add the ones digits and state both the written digit and carry.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: 8 plus 7 is 15, so write 5 and carry 1.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Now add the tens digits including that carry.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: 4 plus 3 plus 1 is 8.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: So which value is mathematically supported?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: 85 is supported.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: What changed between the supported result and your submitted answer?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: The digits were reversed when I copied the result.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Is that an addition misconception or a transcription error? Explain.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: It is a transcription error because the addition in my draft is correct.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Correct the answer, then name one check you can use before submitting.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: The answer is 85. I can compare the answer box with my last draft line.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Use an estimate as a second check: is the total closer to 50 or 90?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: It is closer to 90, so 85 is plausible.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: If the draft had said 58 too, what kind of evidence would we need next?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: We would inspect the addition steps to see whether I misunderstood or miscalculated.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Summarize the error and prevention strategy in your own words.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: I added correctly to get 85 but copied it as 58. I should compare the final box with the last draft line and estimate the size.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Tell me what the problem asks.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: It asks for notebooks sold over two days.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Which operation should you use?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: Addition.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Why addition?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: Because we combine Monday and Tuesday.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Calculate 48 plus 37 again.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: I get 85.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: But your answer is 58. Check your addition.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: The addition in my draft is 85.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Maybe you used subtraction somewhere.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: No, I added both times.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Could you have misunderstood what total means?

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: I think total means combine them.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Then calculate it with a calculator if needed.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: The calculator also says 85.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: So your original answer was wrong and 85 is correct.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: Yes, but I still do not know why I wrote 58.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: You may have made a careless arithmetic mistake.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: But the arithmetic in the draft is correct.

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Be more careful next time and check every step.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: That is vague. Which step should I check?

dialogue_messages.speaker: teacher
dialogue_messages.text: Check the entire solution before submitting.

dialogue_messages.speaker: student
dialogue_messages.text: Okay, but I am not sure what specific habit would prevent this.
